name: The Geologist
description: Iona Lerida reporting for duty as your geologist! I've heard that bedrock is particularly low on this planet, so we'll probably have lots of fun underground.

quests.name: Gems
quests.description: This place is still full of surprises! While gems might be found in ore deep underground on our worlds, here they seem to just be littered everywhere. If you mine out enough stone or throw some gravel or sand onto a sluice, you're bound to find some shinies. Even diamonds can be gotten renewably this way! Gemstones come in 5 different grades, from chipped to exquisite. depending on the quality, they may produce more items. If you need normal grade gems specifically, you can either smash some better ones or try to cut the lower-grade ones into shape.

tasks.longDescription: Send me a specimen of every gem you find! Chipped ones should suffice for now, but I will take any quality.

quests.name: Fire Bricks
quests.description: Fire clay, made from kaolinite and graphite mixed with regular clay, is a very heat resistant material, as the name implies. You'll probably find it useful for creating devices that will have to withstand high temperatures for long amounts of time. If you want to make fire bricks, you can make it quite a bit cheaper by substituting clay for caminite and changing some of the brickwork for nether brick.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following item:

quests.name: One Steel
quests.description: Good job for reaching Steel! I bet it took longer than expected. Well, we expected this adventure to not take much longer than 20 mins or so, yet here we are... Now, you might not want to hear this, but you'll need more. Like way, way more, and this blast furnace you just made is about the best you'll get. A few things to know for when, not if, you'll want to automate it: 1) the tuyere in the furnace controller can and will break over time and cannot be inserted automatically. This means you'll either have to make a tuyere that doesn't degrade, or use a fuel like thermite that burns hot enough to melt steel without needing to be stoked. 2) Fuels show how long they burn IN A FORGE. The blast furnace burns 4 times as much, 8 times if it's stoked with a bellows. use timers to dispense more fuel into the top on these set intervals. 3) once the ore is melted, the molten heap in the chimney will drop in height significantly. since these blocks also emit light, you can use a light sensor to detect this change and insert more ore and flux. You can also use more exotic ways of detection like an ender porcupine + scanner if you don't like the idea of building a dark room over the top of your furnace. Lastly, you'll probably want to insert iron and flux in batches of 20 each.

tasks.longDescription: I think a steel anvil should be an adequate trophy for ya, but since there's other ways to get tier IV smithing, i'll settle on an ingot.

quests.name: Complete Catalogue: Igneous Rock
quests.description: For further analysis, could you get me one of each igneous rock type you can find?

tasks.longDescription: Send me the following items:

quests.name: Types of Rock
quests.description: Unlike homeworld, this planet seems to possess a wide variety of rocks that seem to be stacked in 3 vertical layers. Not only do they each make for stylish building materials, but most ores look like they can only be found in some specific rock types.

tasks.longDescription: For the start, show me a block of cobble, just 4 pebbles in a crafting grid to make some.

quests.name: Sample Sedimentary Rock
quests.description: Sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition of mineral from above, like sand being made from the ground up husks of seashells that sink to the ocean floor. As a result, it can only be found as the top layer, aka the ground directly beneath your feet.

tasks.longDescription: Show me some sedimentary rock

quests.name: Better(?) tools
quests.description: If you're bored out of your mind with the standard tools you've been making from casting and forging metal, you can make a wooden sword and log mallet. Dr. Mickelus has come up with a new way of making modular tools, even metal and diamond ones, without needing a smeltery just yet: While those two tools are generally useless on their own, you can make a workbench by using the mallet on a vanilla crafting table to upgrade them into whatever you like. just select the toolparts you want and craft them using the materials you have. this will necessitate that you upgrade a spare set of tools (hammer, sword, and axe) that you use to craft the other tools. So, for instance, to get a stone hammer for tier 2 smithing, you'll need to upgrade one log mallet with stone while having the other one in your inventory, then switch and upgrade the other one to tier 3, and so on. Besides the inherent modularity, this method also means that some of your smithing can be more precise, allowing for some unique attachments like the claw or sickle. By pressing the "Excavate" Key, you can also use the tool to induce a resonance catastrophe in nearby material, breaking up to 20 blocks(of the same material) at once. However, these tools have tiny amounts of durability compared to even a cast bronze tool, and if you want to repair it fully, you'll have to expend one of each material you've made your toolparts out of.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you've made the following items:

quests.name: Caminite
quests.description: Caminite is a simple blend of clay and sand, and very heat resistant. It's an eccelent thermal insulator and is best used for applications where the heat produced cannot be lost, either due to expensive fuels, strict temperature margins, or if the heat was valuable in some other way.

tasks.longDescription: Caminite needs utmost care while hardening, so using the gentle heat of an oven would be your best bet until you find something that can replicate that process.

quests.name: Complete Catalogue: Sedimentary Rock
quests.description: For further analysis, could you get me one of each sedimentary rock type you can find?

tasks.longDescription: Send me the following items:

quests.name: Sample Igneous Rock
quests.description: Igneous rocks are rocks that have been formed by the cooling of lava or magma. they come in intrusive and extrusive form. I'm curious if there's any on this planet at all. If not, that would be stange. All rock layers should be able to contain this group of minerals, and the bottom layer should be comprised entirely of it, so it shouldn't be hard to find.

tasks.longDescription: Show me some igneous rock

quests.name: Two Steel
quests.description: Useful for its light absorbing properties and hardness, this alloy is essential for heavy-duty machinery and things like radiators, though you will probably first put it to use for forging higher-tier materials. You make it by first alloying black bronze, nickel and steel into weak steel and welding that with a pig iron ingot, then working the result. This process is lossy however: one ingot of black steel is made for every weak steel and  pig iron ingot you combine. I am sure that things like an automatic anvil will yield better results.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made the following item:

quests.name: Flux
quests.description: Metallurgic flux is one of the most important substances in the field of blacksmithing, preventing welds from oxidizing and to bind slag when making steel. You can either grind up some marble, dolomite, limestone or chalk to get it, or gather some seashells from the shores. As you'll develop industry down there, you'll probably want to find a way to get it in a renewable fashion, or at least extract flux rock from the ground in massive quantities, aka build some sort of quarry.

tasks.longDescription: Most likely, you'll also want a quern as it makes it possible to get flux from seashells and is used as a simple grinder for other recipes.

quests.name: Quarrying
quests.description: Simple pebbles and cobblestone won't do for our operations, we'll need some raw and polished stone. The latter is quite intuitive to obtain, simply chisel a block of naturally occuring raw rock while holding a hammer in your other hand. After that, the polished stone can be mined like normal. To obtain the raw rock, you'll have to carve it out by mining the 6 blocks around it.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained these items:

quests.name: Making Glass
quests.description: To make glass, we will need a Smeltery and some Silica Sand, which means either Quartzite, Granite, Chert, Phyllite or Rhyolite Sand, aka the same ones from which you can get nether quartz. then, throw it into the cauldron together with some potash and lime, wait for it to heat up, and take it out using either a mold or blowpipe.

tasks.longDescription: Send me the following items:

quests.name: Red Steel
quests.description: This Complex Alloy has a peculiar structure that allows it to behave like a super-inductor. Useful for high-tech Coils.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following item:

quests.name: Mining and Prospecting
quests.description: You may have guessed it, those tiny lumps of metal aren't going to suffice for any real endeavor of ours. Fortunately, they hint at bigger veins underground that are capable of yielding multiple stacks of ingots of you mine them out entirely. If you want to know how close you are to a vein, make a prospector's pick and use it on the ground to get a rough estimate of the mineral concentration around you. Note that it never reports false positives, only false negatives, so if nothing shows up the first time, try another block before thinking of leaving.

tasks.longDescription: Get some torches and ladders while you're at it. Support beams will also come in handy to, ya know, not bring down the ceiling instantly.

quests.name: Blue Steel
quests.description: This Complex Alloy has next to no inductive or capacitive properties, but does boast quite the high resistance. Useful for laying dense wiring with lots of criss-crossing lines. In other words, perfect for circuit boards.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following item:

quests.name: Sample Metamorphic Rock
quests.description: Metamorphic rocks are characterized by having been rearranged in some way under intense pressures, the original rock isn't important for this definition. If this place has them, that would mean that there are areas with intense pressures, so a healthy amount of geological and tectonic activity. It can be found in the top two rock layers.

tasks.longDescription: Show me some metamorphic rock.
